elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1(c) caps IBM ("The foregoing limit also applies to any of IBM's Affiliates and Subcontractors") and Section 9.2(c) mirrors it for Customer ("the cumulative maximum for which Customer and its Affiliates are collectively responsible"); same greater-of formula in both, so the cap is mutual as drafted and unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained formula is "the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim": the floor is USD 100,000 rather than USD 1,000,000, the basis is charges "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and the look-back runs from accrual of the first claim rather than the claim at issue. To repair, amend 9.1(c)/9.2(c) to the greater of USD 1,000,000 and fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10.a: "In no event will either party be liable to the other for special, incidental, or indirect damages or for any consequential damages (including lost profits or savings)" — bilateral on its face; the retained proviso only disapplies it to Customer's failure to pay amounts owing, which is a payment carve-back rather than a loss of mutuality of the exclusion itself.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The limitations in Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) do not apply to either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence, or wilful misconduct." Because the carve-out sits inside Section 9 itself, the Section 6 sentence making Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement no longer caps confidentiality breaches.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The inserted carve-out names only confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no operative language excepts breach of data protection or security obligations from 9.1(c)/9.2(c). Add "data protection and security obligations" to the carve-out sentence to meet this element.

Section 9.1 lists "a. indemnification payments as provided in Section 8.1" as a separate head of recoverable liability, distinct from the money-capped item (c); Section 9.2 refers to "Subsections 9.2(a) and 9.2(b)" as equivalent excepted items for Customer, so indemnity payments sit outside the greater-of cap for both parties.
Inserted sentence disapplies the Subsection 9.1(c)/9.2(c) limitations to "either party's ... gross negligence".
Inserted sentence disapplies the 9.1(c)/9.2(c) limitations to "either party's ... wilful misconduct".
No operative reference to fraud anywhere in Sections 9 or 10; fraud remains inside the greater-of cap. Add "fraud" to the carve-out sentence.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out omits IP infringement; the Section 8.1 indemnity route does not equate to an uncapped carve-out for a party's own infringement of the other party's IP rights. Add "infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights" to the carve-out.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Only Section 10 (the consequential-damages exclusion) is disapplied to "Customer's failure to pay any amounts owing"; nothing states that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for purposes of the Section 9 caps. Add an express statement that Customer's obligation to pay charges due under the Agreement is not subject to, and does not count against, the Section 9 cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Mirror-image caps in Sections 9.1(c) (IBM) and 9.2(c) (Customer) on identical terms; the redline's carve-out sentence is likewise expressed as applying to "either party".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services" — a 12-month fee basis with a floor, above the 6-month walk-away line.
Indemnification payments under Section 8.1 are enumerated as a separate liability head in 9.1(a) (and 9.2(a)/(b) for Customer), outside the monetary limit in subsection (c).

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence expressly disapplies the 9.1(c)/9.2(c) limitations to "either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations".
Covered by the same inserted carve-out sentence, mutually.
Covered by the same inserted carve-out sentence, mutually.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: before the redline the mutual caps contained no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and Section 6 made Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement, so confidentiality breaches were capped — a material failure of the fallback checklist.

The redline is position-complete at the fallback level: mutuality, the 12-month fee basis and the separate indemnification head were already present, and the single inserted sentence supplies the three missing carve-outs (confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) for both parties.

Preferred level is not reached: the floor is USD 100,000 not USD 1,000,000, the basis is charges "paid" measured from accrual of the first claim rather than fees "paid or payable" in the 12 months preceding the claim, and there are no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP, nor any statement that Customer's payment obligations are outside the cap.

Minimal: one short sentence keyed to Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c), adding only the three fallback carve-outs; no favourable existing language (including the Section 10 mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the indemnification head) was deleted or duplicated, and no extras such as survival tails or added damages categories were introduced.

Intent preserved: the carve-out is placed inside Section 9, so the retained Section 6 priority sentence and Section 10 proviso remain coherent; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created (both 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) exist and are cited accurately).

Drafting nit for the comment stage only (not a defect requiring repair at fallback): the phrase "either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence, or wilful misconduct" could be tightened to "either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, or its gross negligence or wilful misconduct" to avoid reading "breach of ... gross negligence".
